text: We all know it's not sentient, but for some reason it still hurts to read. Spike Jonze's IKEA commercial played on the exact same human tendency: [VIDEO]

story: Apple apologizes for iPad 'Crush' ad that 'missed the mark'
text: If it weren't offensive to someone, somewhere, they wouldn't do it. Apple, on the other hand, will never be punk. They left that path when they realized it was more profitable to become the guy on the screen in their earlier ad. A better comparison might be to Spike Jonze's famous Ikea ad ( [VIDEO] ), which was also sort of disturbing to watch.

story: Apparent signs of distress during LLM redteaming
text: Right, humans anthropomorphize things super easily, which IKEA exploited in this famous ad: [VIDEO] Now we’re spending billions of dollars to build the most anthropomorphic machines we can possibly create. Of course it’s going to mess with us, even if we know it’s happening. Another great and relevant scene: [LINK]

story: McDonald's pulls AI Christmas ad after backlash
text: Who cares if it's AI made or not. It's funny even as it is offensive to many. One thing I've always wondered, with outrage over ads like this, would this (old) ad now be considered funny or offensive? [VIDEO]

story: The IKEA catalogue through the ages
text: Given IKEA essentially produce throwaway furniture by design, I don't think they've got much of a leg to stand on when it comes to environmental responsibility. Just buying more stuff is literally how they have historically marketed themselves. [VIDEO]
